title: A channel post becomes a message with exactly one attachment and retention by attachment

story.i_want_to: have every message attached to exactly one thing (a work item's thread, one session's DMs, or a repo channel) and kept exactly as long as that thing needs it
story.so_that: no message lingers unattached and no reader has to guess which sub-channel a message lives in

rationale: PRD R11: 'All messages, if they don't get attached to session/item, get swiped like unused memory', and section 4 refactors channel_posts into messages rather than adding a store beside it. Today a channel_posts row has only project_id (lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_post.ex:177-244), a uniform 30-day expires_at (Coordination @retention_days, lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:46), and an optional keyed working-state slot that PRD section 4 folds into work-item notes, except handoff:<anchor> slots, which keep their key, index and 30 days until release 7. Ordering today is the global seq bigserial, assigned before commit, which is why every delta read needs a 5 s look-back (coordination.ex:248-282); a cursor read (US-52.24) needs an order that equals commit order.

acceptance_criteria.description: channel_posts gains story_id (FK stories ON DELETE CASCADE), to_holder_id (FK holders ON DELETE CASCADE) and author_holder_id (FK holders ON DELETE SET NULL), project_id becomes nullable, and the check constraint channel_posts_one_attachment admits exactly three shapes: a thread (story_id and the story's project_id set, to_holder_id null), a DM (to_holder_id set, story_id and project_id null), or a channel (project_id alone); the context sets all four columns, none is cast.

Every insert into channel_posts goes through Loopctl.Coordination.Messages.insert/2, which takes pg_advisory_xact_lock on the attachment and sets attachment_seq to the attachment's current maximum plus one, under the unique index channel_posts_attachment_seq_uidx on (tenant_id, COALESCE(story_id, to_holder_id, project_id), attachment_seq); two concurrent inserts on one attachment get consecutive values that commit in that order.

expires_at is set from the attachment at insert: NULL for a thread or a DM; now + the tenant setting channel_message_retention_days (default 7) for a channel message; now + Coordination.retention_days/0 (30) for a channel row keyed handoff:<anchor>. ChannelPostSweeper's predicate (expires_at < now) is unchanged, so thread and DM rows are never swept by age.

The migration backfills attachment_seq for every existing row per project in (inserted_at, seq) order, and sets expires_at = LEAST(expires_at, inserted_at + interval '7 days') on every existing channel row whose key does not start handoff:.

A write carrying a key that does not start handoff: is refused with 422 code keyed_slot_retired, whose message says working state is work-item notes written with the notes verb; the migration sets key = NULL on every existing non-handoff keyed row, and channel_posts_session_key_uidx is rebuilt with the predicate key LIKE 'handoff:%'.

Loopctl.Delivery.EscalationInbox.post_project/5 dedupes its digest through idempotency_key = digest_key/2 on a keyless channel message instead of a keyed slot, and a second post for the same project and day still answers :already_posted.

Every channel read (Coordination.recent_page/3, directed_handoffs_page/3, get_post/2 and the graduate and delete paths) returns only channel-attached rows of the caller's tenant: a thread message or a DM is never returned by a channel read, by id or by list.

Projects.Merge.merge_into/4 moves the source project's channel and thread messages to the target and renumbers the moved channel messages' attachment_seq after the target channel's last, in their old order, so channel_posts_attachment_seq_uidx never reports a merge conflict.

test_cases.name: the one-attachment check admits three shapes and refuses the rest (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant, project, story in project (fixture(:story)), holder = fixture(:holder) (provided by release 3, US-52.13)
steps: insert through AdminRepo: story_id + project_id; to_holder_id alone; project_id alone; story_id + to_holder_id; nothing; story_id without project_id
expected_results: first three succeed; the last three raise a check violation on channel_posts_one_attachment

test_cases.name: concurrent inserts on one attachment commit in attachment_seq order (DataCase, async: false: two committed transactions racing, moduledoc says why)
preconditions: one channel; Loopctl.Test.ProductionTopology for a second connection
steps: start transaction T1 and insert through Messages.insert/2 without committing
start T2 and insert on the same channel (it waits on the advisory lock)
expected_results: T1's row has attachment_seq n, T2's n + 1; T2 never commits before T1

test_cases.name: retention by attachment (DataCase)
preconditions: tenant settings %{"channel_message_retention_days" => 3} on a second tenant; default on the first
steps: insert a thread message, a DM, a channel message and a handoff:repo#1 channel post in the first tenant
insert a channel message in the second tenant
run ChannelPostSweeper with the clock 31 days ahead
expected_results: expires_at nil, nil, now+7d, now+30d; second tenant now+3d; after the sweep only the thread message and the DM remain

test_cases.name: migration backfill, retention clamp and keyed-slot fold (DataCase migration test)
preconditions: rows in two projects: keyless posts 20 and 2 days old, a keyed session_goal slot, a handoff:repo#7 post
expected_results: attachment_seq 1..n per project in insertion order; the 20-day post now expired; session_goal row key NULL; handoff row unchanged with its key and 30-day expires_at

test_cases.name: a non-handoff key is refused; a handoff key still upserts (ConnCase)
preconditions: agent key that is a writable member of the project
expected_results: 422 code keyed_slot_retired; 201 then 200 on one row

test_cases.name: escalation digest dedupes on its idempotency key (DataCase)
steps: run the digest twice for the same day
expected_results: one keyless channel message with idempotency_key = digest_key; second run :already_posted

test_cases.name: channel reads never return thread or DM rows, nor another tenant's (DataCase)
preconditions: in tenant A: a channel message, a thread message and a DM on one project; tenant B with an agent

test_cases.name: merge renumbers moved channel messages (DataCase)
preconditions: source channel with attachment_seq 1..3, target channel with 1..2, a thread message in the source
expected_results: target channel holds seq 1..5, the source's three as 3..5 in their old order; the thread message keeps its story_id and attachment_seq

technical_notes: Schema: lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_post.ex:177-244; create_changeset/2 :286 requires project_id at :307, which becomes required only for thread and channel rows. Holders table and fixture(:holder): provided by US-52.13 (holders, schema Loopctl.Holders.Holder).

Messages.insert/2 lives in lib/loopctl/coordination/messages.ex (Loopctl.Coordination.Messages), a submodule of the context that owns channel_posts, not a new context: Coordination.post/4 (coordination.ex:648, run_post/5 :3073) and create_post/4 (:421) both call it for their inserts. Lock key: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(tenant_id || attachment_id, 0)). A keyed handoff upsert that hits an existing row keeps its attachment_seq.

Why a per-attachment counter and not the global seq: seq (channel_post.ex:241) is assigned pre-commit, so a later seq can commit first; @commit_lag_epsilon_seconds (coordination.ex:282) exists only to paper over that, and a cursor that must never skip cannot rely on it.

Tenant setting channel_message_retention_days is read with Tenants.get_tenant_settings/3 (lib/loopctl/tenants.ex:1191); the default 7 is one module attribute in Messages, referenced by the OpenAPI text.

Readers of the changed rows, each filtered to channel attachments (story_id IS NULL AND to_holder_id IS NULL): recent_page/3 coordination.ex:3571 (query :3584), directed_handoffs_page/3 :3769 (:3788), get_post/2 :2798, delete_post/5 :2610, graduate_post/4 :2869, list_quarantined_posts/2 :2654 (stays all attachments: it is the operator's review of every row), EscalationHandoffs queries lib/loopctl/delivery/escalation_handoffs.ex:134, :366, :538 (handoff: rows, channel-attached by construction), ChannelPostRescanWorker (scans every attachment), IngestionHealth's retention-stall read system_retention_stall_candidates/2 coordination.ex:342 (expires_at IS NULL rows are never residue), and claude-config hooks/session-start.sh:475 (reads GET /channel/posts, channel rows only).

Keyed-slot callers: EscalationInbox.post_project/5 lib/loopctl/delivery/escalation_inbox.ex:634-656 (digest_key/2 :569, @digest_session :102) is the only server-side non-handoff keyed writer; EscalationHandoffs (escalation_handoffs.ex:402) writes handoff: keys and is unchanged. maybe_derive_handoff_key/1 (coordination.ex:757) stays.

keyed_slot_retired message: 'keyed working-state slots are retired: write plan, progress, decisions and questions as work-item notes (story_notes, release 3), and messages with message_send'. Add the 422 to ChannelPostController.create operation/2 (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/channel_post_controller.ex:892) and CHANGELOG.md.

Merge: lib/loopctl/projects/merge.ex:41-63; update the channel_posts_session_key_uidx entry's where to key LIKE 'handoff:%'; renumbering runs in the merge transaction after the move, under the target channel's advisory lock.

Migration: name it after git fetch origin; the backfill uses row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id, project_id ORDER BY inserted_at, seq). Rebuild indexes CONCURRENTLY is not possible inside the transaction; the table is small (30-day TTL).
non_goals: The send API and MCP tool for threads and DMs: US-52.23.
Cursor reads and the inbox: US-52.24.
Deleting handoff: posts and their slot index: release 7 (README names table: move verb).

failure_modes.partition: n/a: every write and read here is one transaction against loopctl's own Postgres inside the request; nothing crosses a second service.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.22.1 and AC-52.22.3: a message's attachment and lifetime are columns of its row, so a restart or deploy changes neither; a thread dies only with its story (FK cascade).
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.22.2: attachment_seq is taken inside the insert's transaction, so a rolled-back attempt consumes nothing and a retry takes the next value once; AC-52.22.6: the digest's retry is deduped by its idempotency key.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.22.2: a slow writer holding an attachment's advisory lock delays later writes on that one attachment and never reorders them; other attachments do not wait.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: inline in the request process; the age sweep is the existing ChannelPostSweeper cron, unchanged.

definition_of_done: On production after the migration: SELECT count(*) FROM channel_posts WHERE key IS NOT NULL AND key NOT LIKE 'handoff:%' returns 0, and SELECT count(*) FROM channel_posts WHERE attachment_seq IS NULL returns 0.
defaults: Channel message retention: 7 days, tenant setting channel_message_retention_days (owner may change).
Existing channel posts are clamped to the new 7-day window at migration; handoff: posts keep 30 days until release 7.
Existing non-handoff keyed slots become plain channel messages (they have no work item to attach to).
